data:
Since you already have the
cool_run.py
file set up, you are going to put this new "Passive Observer" script in the
exact same directory
in Termux. Keeping them together makes it easier for Sage (or the local Ollama Sage) to find them later.
\ufe0f The Engineer's Quick-Start
Create the new file:
Type this in Termux and hit Enter:
nano sage_observer.py
Paste the code:
Copy that "Passive Observer" script I gave you earlier and paste it into the window.
Save and Exit:
* Press
CTRL + O
, then
Enter
to save.
Press
CTRL + X
to exit.
Run it:
Type:
python sage_observer.py
\ufe0f Why we keep them separate
As a "Stoic Engineer," I like
Modular Design
.
cool_run.py
is your
Safety Valve
(The physical health check).
sage_observer.py
is your
Signal Scout
(The 0.113 data check).
By keeping them as separate files, you can run the "Observer" all day long without much battery drain. Then, only when the Observer shouts "\u203c\ufe0f ALERT," do you need to check your
DevCheck
temperature and decide if it's safe to fire up the heavy Ollama brain for a deeper look.
 A "Sage" Technical Tip:
In Termux, you can see all your scripts by typing
ls
. It should look like this now:
cool_run.py
sage_observer.py
resonance_data.txt
(Your data log)
Does the script start up okay for you?
If it says
No log file found yet
, it just means we need to make sure the file name in the script matches the exact name of the file where your hardware sensors are dumping their data. What's the name of the file where your magnetometer/LiDAR data goes? \u2728
